what: Consolidated checkpoint for the Option A revision: exact identifiability, the extraction-tolerance frontier, the kappa correction, the pre-registered kappa noise test, the phantom census, and the ladder under both reference points. Source of record for every red-marked value in manuscript/revised_new.

ck_1_1_kappa.definition: kappa = max over enumerated independent view pairs of ||[P_v; P_w]^+||_2 (Proposition 2)
ck_1_1_kappa.superseded_value_diagnosis: 1.7689 = 1.33^2; 1.328 is the kappa of pairs axis_c|body_diagonal and axis_c|oblique2, so a squaring slip is the likely origin. No formulation tested (stacked, transposed, hstacked, Frobenius, sigma_max/sigma_min) reproduces 1.7689.

ck_2_1_kappa_prediction.prediction_rule: Proposition 2 band: structure safe iff |d_compared - tau| > 2*kappa*eps. With d_min >> tau, eps_tol = (d_min - tau)/(2*kappa). sigma* for R1>=0.95 predicted as the 5th percentile of eps_tol over structures.
ck_2_1_kappa_prediction.falsifiable_content: If kappa governs noise robustness, the measured crossing sigma must order the three protocols as predicted_robustness_ordering, and off-axis must cross at roughly 3.08x lower sigma than frozen (the kappa ratio, since d_min is identical for both).

verdict.reading:
Mixed, and reported as such. TWO of the three predictions fail and one holds.
(1) HOLDS - the kappa-isolating contrast. Frozen and off-axis differ only in camera placement, so kappa alone separates them, and the predicted direction is observed: frozen crosses R1 = 0.95 at sigma = 0.0146 against 0.0069 for off-axis, a factor of 2.1 where kappa predicted 3.1. The paired test confirms it at sigma = 0.01 (18 structures frozen-only against 3 off-axis-only, p = 0.0015) and sigma = 0.02 (102 against 2, p = 5.4e-28). Raising kappa 3.08-fold by perturbing the cameras off the principal axes costs noise robustness, as Proposition 2 requires.
(2) FAILS - the three-way ordering. Tiled was predicted second and is measured last (crossing at sigma = 0.0048). The prediction treated tiling as a kappa-preserving change, which it is not: tiling multiplies atoms per cell eightfold and shrinks same-species separations, so it degrades robustness through atom density rather than through camera conditioning. The prediction was mis-specified for that arm, and the arm cannot score kappa in either direction.
(3) FAILS - the absolute sigma*. Predicted 0.4456 for frozen against 0.0146 observed, optimistic by a factor of 31. The prediction used the minimum same-species interatomic distance as the margin, but the binding constraint is the much smaller displacement at which spglib's symmetry detection flips. Proposition 2's band is sufficient for label agreement, not tight, so it orders conditioning correctly and bounds absolute tolerance loosely.
What the paper may claim from this: kappa predicts the RELATIVE noise robustness of two protocols that differ only in camera placement. It does not predict robustness across protocols that differ in atom density, and it does not give a usable absolute noise budget.

kappa_isolating_contrast.why: identical structures and identical atom geometry; the ONLY difference is camera placement, hence kappa. The tiled arm changes the geometry itself (8x atoms per cell, smaller same-species separations), so it is not a controlled kappa contrast and cannot score the prediction either way.

ck_2_3_phantoms1933.density_dependence_reading: The pooled Spearman of phantom count against atoms per cell has OPPOSITE SIGNS at two views (+0.4571) and three views (-0.1471), so a single rate would misreport it. Decomposing resolves the sign flip. Conditional on Phi_0 being nonempty, count rises steeply with atoms per cell at both view counts (rho 0.8331 at two views, n=1408; rho 0.8273 at three, n=365). What differs is the probability of being nonempty at all: flat in atoms at two views (rho 0.0299, p = 0.19) but DECREASING at three (rho -0.1875, p = 6.9e-17). The three-view pooled negative is therefore a mixture effect - larger cells are less likely to admit any phantom under three-view verification, but produce many when they do - and not evidence that density protects against phantoms. This is the measurement the method section promises in place of a proved rate; we report the decomposition rather than a single coefficient.
ck_2_3_phantoms1933.note_on_binned_means: The binned means at three views (2.143, 0.530, 10.135, 5.083 across 0-20, 20-40, 40-60, 60-100 atoms) are non-monotone because only 18.72% of structures have any phantom at three views, so each bin mean is dominated by zeros and a few large counts. The conditional statistics above are the interpretable form; the bin means are reported for completeness only.

over_merge_diagnostic.what: The 10 structures the released pipeline tolerance (delta=0.15) misclassifies on the original sample.
over_merge_diagnostic.reading: Each of the 10 recovers the right number of atoms and has its closest same-species pair at least 1.7251 A apart, over eleven times delta, so the failures are over-merging of distinct atoms by the merge step rather than the projection coincidences of Phi_tau.
